history.p: The first sign of Gade working on the sonata goes back to September 1839, when he entered it in his so-called "composer's diary". According to this entry he was inspired by poems by Ernst Schulze and Friedrich Schlegel. However, he did not start composing until November that year, but then worked on it for fifteen years. When the sonata was published in 1854, it was dedicated to Franz Liszt, who through Gade's father-in-law, J.P.E. Hartmann, acknowledged the dedication calling the sonata "beautiful", but apparently never performed it in public.

physDesc.physMedium: 3 bifolios and 2 single folios. Written in ink with numerous cancellations and emendations in pencil and ink. Paper: 14 staves. Paginated 1-16. Heading on p. 1 "Sonate". At the the beginning of the second movement on p. 8 stave 3, dated "29/1 - 39". At the beginning of the Scherzo, on p. 11 dated "9/12. 39".
